summary:
SL-103 passes on everything I could run.

**Code-level checks of the guards** (contact: code):
- The whole suite passes, 935/935.
- rules-parity says AGREE, byte-identical to before: 18 facts, 22 twinned entries, 48 patterns.
- RuleCases C-001, C-003, C-004 and C-005 hold.
- rules-harness: clean baseline CLEAN (91 rules, 225 files, 0 hits). All 16 touched plants read AS-RECORDED with 0 stray hits, including F51 (RegDelete prefix), S53, S54 and S55 (/v branch), S56 and S57.

**The pre-fix proof is repeatable.** I followed the corpus's own `closed_by.how_to_repeat` recipe in a scratch copy:
- The two pattern files were restored blob-exact from 1105c3f; the HEAD corpus and test file were kept.
- The corpus test failed exactly 42 rows, the same set as `closed_by.ids`, with no differences either way.
- 83 tests passed, including TheCorpusHolds… (counts 9/6).

**Fitness agrees with the corpus on every row.** I ran the real taad3 Fitness engine with one file per corpus row:
- It agrees on 124 of 124 rows, with 0 hits outside the planted files or in the wrong scope.
- The RegDelete/SHDelete prefix rows (B45–B50) fire.
- W58 (/v) fires, and so do W57 and W60. W56, W59, W53, W54, W69 and W70 stay at 0, as their miss rows record.
- The 63 SL-091 rows are unchanged, and every new row has before=quiet.

**Run-time membership** (contact: real). I measured this in Windows Sandbox (build 26100, PowerShell 5.1, as SYSTEM, so in SYSTEM's own HKCU):
- The new fire rows really change Hidden or ShowSuperHidden: W48, W51, W52, W55, W58, W61, W62 (Copy-ItemProperty overwrites an existing Hidden), W63, W64, and W65–W67 through FromHandle.
- The quiet rows W44, W47, W68 and W73 cannot write.
- The miss rows W56 (regedit /s) and W59 (WMI) are real write routes, correctly pinned as outside the bound.

**Key-level rows.** W49, W50 and W60 were refused on SYSTEM's own Explorer\Advanced. On a scratch key of the same shape, Remove-Item and DeleteSubKeyTree remove the key, and New-Item -Force recreates it empty, values and subkeys gone. That last result measures the corpus's #5444 run_time_fact, which until now was only cited.

**Design departures, declared and accepted:**
- CreateSubKey is not a write marker, on measurement.
- W60 moved from miss to fire under review M1.
- The before-fix set is 42 ids, not the 33 the design predicted (46 rows planned, 61 added).

**Already filed.** Rename-Item and Move-Item of the key, reg copy, Start-Process reg import, and New-Item -Name Advanced -Force (O-024 to O-028) are real writes the guard lets through. They are waived to the backlog and do not hold this slice.

checks.evidence: Passed! Failed 0, Passed 935, Skipped 0, Total 935, 24 s, exit 0. That is 874 + 61 new corpus rows, so every corpus row, including B49 and W56–W60, passes in xUnit.

checks.what: rules-parity: twinned yaml entry and Fact still agree
checks.evidence: rules-parity: AGREE 18 facts <- 22 twinned entries, 48 patterns; 69 settled entries not compared. exit 0.
Each ended 'All checks held.', exit 0. C-001: AGREE 18 facts. C-003: 70 settled after the appended entry. C-004 and C-005 hit their DRIFT and CANNOT-READ controls as intended.

checks.what: rules-harness on the 16 touched plants (4 old + 12 new)
checks.evidence: Clean baseline: xunit 18 Facts, 0 hits; fitness 91 rules, 225 files read, 0 hits, none unmatched → CLEAN. 16 rows, 16 AS-RECORDED, 0 stray hits, exit 0. F49, F50 and F51 are fire/fire; P34 and P35 are quiet/quiet; S51 and S53–S57 are xunit quiet and fitness fire; S52 is quiet. The one import rule is NOT RUN, as the harness always reports.

checks.what: Before-fix proof repeated independently, following the corpus's closed_by.how_to_repeat recipe
checks.command: Robocopy of the worktree to %TEMP%\sl103-val. .taad/fitness.yaml and ArchitectureRulesTests.cs restored with `git show 1105c3f:<path>` (git hash-object equals the 1105c3f blob for both). HEAD corpus and test file kept. eng/dotnet.ps1 test ... --filter FullyQualifiedName~ExplorerSettingsWriteRuleTests --logger trx
checks.evidence: Failed 42, Passed 83, Total 125, test exit 1, which is the expected failure. Failed ids: B30 B31 B33-B37 B40 B42-B50 W35-W43 W46 W48-W52 W57 W58 W60-W67. Comparing with closed_by.ids (42) gives an empty difference both ways. TheCorpusHoldsRowsTheDeclaredPatternsLetThroughInBothScopes passed, and all 63 SL-091 rows passed under the pre-fix patterns.

checks.what: Real Fitness engine over one file per corpus row, with HEAD's fitness.yaml
checks.command: python fitrows.py (taad3.fitness.check on a scratch tree: src rows as src/FsAnalyser.App/R_<id>.cs; window rows as tests/window/R_<id>.ps1, or tests/window/FsaWindowHook/R_<id>.cs for C# lines; TAAD3_HOME redirected; tree removed)
checks.evidence:
rows=124 agree=124 disagree=0, with 0 hits outside planted rows or in the wrong scope. The only other rule fired is OnlyShellRevealReadsOrOverridesExplorersViewSettings, on planted SHGetSetSettings rows. Focus rows:

checks.what: The 63 SL-091 rows are unchanged, and every new row has before=quiet
checks.command: git diff 1105c3f HEAD -- ExplorerSettingsWriteCorpus.json, plus a JSON compare of rows by id
checks.evidence: Old rows: 63, with 0 changed or missing in line, now, before or scope. The only removed diff lines are the old _note (rewritten per m2) and W34, re-added with a trailing comma. 61 new rows; none has before other than quiet.

checks.what: Run-time membership of the new window rows, Windows Sandbox (build 26100, PS 5.1.26100.9444, SYSTEM's HKCU). Hidden=2, ShowSuperHidden=0 and Sentinel=7 were reset before each line
checks.command: Sandbox script: run each corpus line, plus a FromHandle or managed write for opens, then read Explorer\Advanced (.taad-scratch/sandbox/run-20261012-151309/out/rt.log)
checks.evidence:
Changed (fire rows):
- W48 deleted Hidden.
- W51 and W52 (reg import of a UTF-16 .reg), W55 ('True' + SetValue), W58 (reg add $adv /v Hidden): Hidden 2→1.
- W61 (Clear-Item) removed every value.
- W62 (Copy-ItemProperty) overwrote Hidden 2→1 with no error.
- W63 moved ShowSuperHidden out; W64 renamed Hidden to HiddenOld.
- W65, W66 and W67 + FromHandle: Hidden 2→1. W65 with a managed SetValue threw 'Cannot write to the registry key' (dotnet/runtime#113535).
- Controls W35 and W37: Hidden 2→1.
Unchanged (quiet rows): W68 and W73 + FromHandle threw 'Attempted to perform an unauthorized operation'; W44 the same; W47 threw 'Cannot write to the registry key'; W71 had no effect.
Miss rows W56 (regedit /s) and W59 (WMI StdRegProv): Hidden 2→1. They are real routes, correctly recorded as outside the bound.

checks.what: Key-level rows W49, W50 and W60 on SYSTEM's own Explorer\Advanced in the Sandbox
checks.evidence: Inconclusive, not a slice result. Remove-Item, DeleteSubKeyTree, New-Item -Force, Rename-Item and Move-Item were all refused with UnauthorizedAccessException 'Attempted to perform an unauthorized operation' on SYSTEM's real key. The key had no subkeys, and its ACL is O:SY D:AI(A;CIID;KR;;;BU)(A;CIID;KA;;;BA)(A;CIID;KA;;;SY)(A;CIIOID;KA;;;CO). The cause was not pinned down. These rows were re-measured on a same-shaped scratch key (next check).

checks.what: Key-level semantics on a same-shaped scratch key HKCU\Software\FsaProbe\Explorer\Advanced (with a child subkey), Sandbox
checks.evidence:
- W49 (Remove-Item -Recurse) and W50 (DeleteSubKeyTree): key absent afterwards.
- W60 (New-Item -Force on the existing key): key present but empty, with no values and no subkeys. This measures the corpus's bounded_by.run_time_facts claim (PowerShell/PowerShell#5444), which had only been cited.
- W61 (Clear-Item): values gone, subkey kept.
- W72 (Remove-Item of an unrelated folder): key untouched.
- Control with no action: unchanged.

checks.what: First attempt at the rt2 Sandbox script
checks.evidence: My script had a PowerShell 5.1 parse error: a `foreach` statement piped to Out-File gave 'An empty pipe element is not allowed'. Nothing ran. I fixed it and re-ran (previous check).

checks.what: Waived members O-024, O-025, O-026 and O-028 are real writes (backlog evidence, Sandbox)
checks.evidence:
- Scratch key: Rename-Item and Move-Item of the key leave it absent at its path (O-024). New-Item -Path <Explorer> -Name Advanced -Force recreates it empty (O-028).
- SYSTEM's own key: reg copy from a backup key wrote Hidden 2→1 (O-025). Start-Process reg.exe -ArgumentList 'import',<file> -Wait wrote Hidden 2→1 (O-026).
The code review measured that rule C gives these lines 0 hits. They are already carried to the backlog as SC-313, SC-314, SC-311 and SC-315, so they do not hold the slice.

checks.what: Re-feed the O-024 to O-028 lines to rule C's 9 patterns myself
checks.command: PowerShell: .NET Regex over patterns read from .taad/fitness.yaml
checks.evidence: The engine's PreToolUse guard refused the call. It read the string literals (Rename-Item on HKCU, reg copy) as a settings change, although nothing was going to run them. I did not try to disguise the strings to get past the guard. The code review's own measurement of 0 hits stands for these waived items.

checks.evidence: Junction removed and the worktree's .dotnet\dotnet.exe still present. Scratch removed (True). The two VBCSCompiler processes were from the worktree SDK (15:05) and from my scratch copy (15:10); none is left. git status shows the same 4 entries as at start; the new Sandbox output is under the untracked .taad-scratch/sandbox.

criteria.criterion: 1. Catch a writable open of Explorer\Advanced in src with write-capable RegistryRights: short or qualified, OR'd, behind a check, named argument, OpenBaseKey, or two-backslash path (B30, B31, B33-B37, B40)
criteria.how: These rows failed under the 1105c3f patterns in my scratch re-run, and pass in the HEAD suite (935/935). The real Fitness engine fires each one on its own file (124/124 agree). Harness F49 is fire/fire.

criteria.criterion: 2. Leave a read-only open in src alone: ReadKey (B32), QueryValues (B41), CreateSubKey rights (B38)
criteria.how: These quiet rows pass in xUnit and get 0 Fitness hits. Harness P34 and P35 are quiet/quiet. CreateSubKey is deliberately absent from the marker, as the design decided on the Sandbox measurement RegSetValueExW=5.

criteria.criterion: 3. Catch a delete of Hidden or of the key in src: DeleteValue, DeleteSubKeyTree, RegDeleteValue, RegDeleteKeyValue(W), SHDeleteValue, RegDeleteTree (B42-B49)
criteria.how: B42–B49, plus B50 for DeleteSubKey, failed before the fix and pass now. Each gets 1 Fitness hit. Harness F50 and F51 (RegDelete prefix) are fire/fire. B51 (another value) stays quiet.

criteria.criterion: 4. Record what the src guard cannot see: B39, B27, B28, B29 as miss
criteria.how: The miss rows pass in xUnit with 0 hits and get 0 Fitness hits.

criteria.criterion: 5. Catch a rights open in a window script or the hook (W35, W41, W42, W43)
criteria.how: These failed before and pass now, and fire in Fitness, with W43 as a .cs file under tests/window. In the Sandbox, W35 + FromHandle changed Hidden 2→1.

criteria.criterion: 6. Catch a PowerShell open the author believes is read-only: quoted string as the only second argument (W36, W37, W38, W46)
criteria.how: These failed before and pass now, and fire in Fitness. Harness S51 (W37) reads fitness fire. In the Sandbox, W37 'ReadKey' + managed SetValue changed Hidden 2→1.

criteria.criterion: 7. Catch the cast and all-string open forms (W39, W40)
criteria.how: W39 and W40, plus the M2 rows W65–W67, failed before and fire now in xUnit and Fitness. Harness S57 is fitness fire. In the Sandbox, W65, W66 and W67 + FromHandle each changed Hidden 2→1.

criteria.criterion: 8. Leave a read-only PowerShell open alone (W44, W47, W29); W55 'True' fires as the control
criteria.how: W44, W47, W29, W68 and W73 are quiet in both engines. Harness S52 is quiet/quiet. W55 fires both before and now. In the Sandbox, W44, W68 and W73 + FromHandle threw unauthorized, and W47 + SetValue threw 'Cannot write'; Hidden stayed 2.

criteria.criterion: 9. Catch a delete in a window script or the hook (W48, W49, W50, W57)
criteria.how: These failed before and fire now in both engines. Harness S53 is fitness fire. In the Sandbox, W48 deleted Hidden. W49 and W50 removed the scratch key of the same shape; on SYSTEM's own key they were refused.

criteria.criterion: 10. Catch reg.exe writes wherever the path is held (W51, W52, W58); W09, W10, W11 keep firing
criteria.how: W51, W52 and W58 failed before and fire now. W09, W10 and W11 pass, and were unchanged under the pre-fix run. Harness S54 (import) and S55 (/v) are fitness fire. In the Sandbox, W51, W52 and W58 each changed Hidden 2→1.

criteria.criterion: 11. Record the window routes outside the producer bound: W45, W53, W54, W56, W59, W60
criteria.how: W45, W53, W54, W56 and W59 are miss rows with 0 hits in both engines. The Sandbox shows W56 (regedit /s) and W59 (WMI) really write Hidden, so they are honestly recorded as misses. W60 is no longer a miss: it was flipped to fire under accepted review M1 (O-017 discharged). On the scratch key, New-Item -Force wiped every value and subkey, which supports that flip.

criteria.criterion: 12. Keep every row the SL-091 corpus already settled, their before verdicts, and the 9/6 pattern counts
criteria.how: The 63 old rows are byte-for-byte unchanged in id, line, now, before and scope. They pass under both the 1105c3f and the HEAD patterns. TheCorpusHolds… (9 window, 6 src) passes in both runs.

criteria.criterion: 13. Show the code before the fix failing the rows it closes
criteria.how: I re-ran it independently in a scratch copy with the pattern files restored blob-exact from 1105c3f. Exactly the 42 closed_by ids failed and 83 tests passed. The design's 33 was raised to 42 by the declared M1/M2 rows and B50. The committed how_to_repeat recipe reproduces the run.

criteria.criterion: 14. Both engines and the whole tree agree after the change (Fitness, xUnit twin, rules-parity, harness plants)
criteria.how:
- Suite: 935/935.
- rules-parity: AGREE, unchanged.
- Harness: clean baseline CLEAN (0 hits over today's src and tests/window); 16 rows AS-RECORDED, 0 stray. The design said 14 plants; 16 were run, including S56 and S57 from M1/M2.
- Fitness per row: 124/124 agree.

criteria.criterion: Obligation: the class is answered with a committed corpus path (inputs table, fire/quiet rows, alias list, census, bound, before-fix proof)
criteria.how: tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/ExplorerSettingsWriteCorpus.json has 124 rows and the keys bounded_by, aliases, census and closed_by. The census and alias ids are not machine-checked; that is waived to SC-308.

criteria.criterion: Issue text: widen the marker to include CreateSubKey
criteria.how: This is a deliberate, declared design departure, not a build defect. A Sandbox measurement showed a CreateSubKey-rights handle cannot write Hidden (RegSetValueExW=5), so B38 is quiet. The design's acceptance criteria 1 and 2 govern, and both are met.

obligations.evidence:
The unmeasured texts and rows now behave as predicted:
- RegDelete/SHDelete prefix: B45–B50 pass in xUnit and get 1 hit each from the real Fitness engine. Harness F51 (RegDeleteKeyValueW) is fire/fire, AS-RECORDED.
- /v branch: W58 passes in xUnit and gets 1 Fitness hit. Harness S55 is quiet/fire, AS-RECORDED. W58 has no Explorer\Advanced on the line, so only that branch can fire it, and it failed under the 1105c3f patterns.
- Rows: B49 fire (1 hit). W56 miss (0). W57 fire (1). W58 fire (1). W59 miss (0). W60 fire (1); it was predicted miss in the design and flipped by accepted M1/O-017.
- Plants: S53 and S54 are AS-RECORDED, fitness fire.
The Sandbox also showed W56, W58 and W59 really write Hidden 2→1, and W60's New-Item -Force empties a key of the same shape.

not_reached: An ordinary user's own HKCU\…\Explorer\Advanced. The Sandbox ran as SYSTEM. Key-level deletes and recreates (Remove-Item, DeleteSubKeyTree, New-Item -Force, Rename-Item, Move-Item) were refused on SYSTEM's real key for an unpinned reason, so they were measured on a scratch key of the same shape. The guard verdicts do not depend on this.

The effective Explorer setting (SHGetSetSettings or a fresh Explorer window) after each Sandbox write was not re-read. Only the registry values were. The investigation's earlier showAll 1→0 measurement covers only deleting Hidden.

Run-time behaviour under pwsh 7, which the window scripts may run under. The Sandbox has only Windows PowerShell 5.1. The investigation's round 1 measured the same handle behaviour on pwsh 7.6 / .NET 10.0.12.
Windows 10. Every measurement was on Windows 11 (host 26200, Sandbox 26100).
A rule hit in the repo's real multi-line layout: plants and rows are one line each (waived, SC-310).
Fitness on a UTF-16LE .reg file's content (W53, W54). That needs the taad_v3 engine to decode UTF-16, which is outside this repo.
Whether a managed key.SetValue after a RegistryRights open becomes a real write once dotnet/runtime#113535 ships. No runtime carries it.
